summary: Specifies a SIP extension for reliable provisional responses using the option tag 100rel, and defines the PRACK method that acknowledges them. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3262 adds a way for SIP endpoints to confirm that provisional responses, such as call-progress messages, arrived. The sender numbers and retransmits a response until the other endpoint sends a matching PRACK.

questions: what is a reliable provisional response
subtitle: How SIP confirms delivery of provisional responses using PRACK.

tldr.problem: SIP provisional responses report progress but are not sent reliably by the base specification.
tldr.mechanism: The 100rel option tag enables reliable provisional responses. The sender numbers and retransmits each response until a PRACK names it in an RAck header.
tldr.outcome: SIP gains the PRACK method and the RSeq and RAck headers. RFC 3262 obsoletes RFC 2543.

today: RFC 3262 is a Proposed Standard published in July 2002. It obsoletes RFC 2543; the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 3262.

sections.title: Why Provisional Responses Need Reliability
sections.content:
SIP final responses report the result of a request and are sent reliably. Provisional responses report progress and are not sent reliably in the base SIP specification.

RFC 3262 adds an optional extension for reliable provisional responses. The mechanism retransmits a response with exponential backoff and stops when a matching PRACK arrives.
sections.plainLanguage: A provisional response reports progress before a request is complete. This extension lets the sender repeat it until the recipient confirms receipt.

sections.title: The 100rel Tag, RSeq, and PRACK
sections.content:
The 100rel option tag indicates support for reliable provisional responses. Each such response carries an RSeq sequence number, and the PRACK request carries an RAck header identifying the response by its sequence number and the related CSeq number and method.

Acknowledgements are not cumulative. The RFC recommends keeping only one reliable provisional response outstanding at a time to support congestion control.
sections.plainLanguage: RSeq numbers the response, and RAck identifies which response PRACK confirms. Each response needs its own acknowledgement.

sections.title: Sending Reliable Provisional Responses
sections.content:
A UAS may send a non-100 provisional response reliably when the INVITE indicates support with Supported: 100rel. If the INVITE requires 100rel, the UAS must send each non-100 provisional response reliably or reject the request.

A reliable response includes Require: 100rel and RSeq. The first RSeq is between 1 and 2**31 - 1; later values increase by exactly one and do not wrap. Retransmissions start at T1 and double until a matching PRACK arrives.
sections.plainLanguage: The server marks each reliable provisional response and assigns it a sequence number. It repeats the response with increasing intervals until the matching PRACK arrives.

sections.title: Receiving and Acknowledging Responses
sections.content:
A caller can require reliable provisional responses with Require: 100rel or advertise support with Supported: 100rel. When a qualifying response arrives, the caller creates a PRACK in the response's dialog.

The caller tracks the most recent in-order RSeq. It discards retransmissions and must not process or acknowledge a later response whose RSeq is not exactly one higher than the previous in-order value.
sections.plainLanguage: The caller sends PRACK for each reliable provisional response. If a sequence number is missing, it waits rather than acknowledging a later response out of order.

sections.title: Exchanging Session Descriptions
sections.content:
Reliable provisional responses and PRACK create additional opportunities to exchange session descriptions. A reliable provisional response may carry an answer to an offer in the INVITE, or the first reliable provisional response must carry an offer when the INVITE had none.

If the UAS has sent a session description in a reliable provisional response, it must wait for its acknowledgement before sending a successful final response to the INVITE.
sections.plainLanguage: Endpoints can agree on session details before the call receives its final response. The server waits for acknowledgement when a provisional response carries a session description.

sections.title: Authenticating PRACK
sections.content:
An attacker could inject a PRACK and cause the UAS to stop retransmitting a reliable provisional response. These responses may carry important information.

The RFC says PRACK messages should be authenticated like other SIP requests, using the procedures defined by the base SIP specification.
sections.plainLanguage: A forged PRACK could stop a response from being repeated. The RFC recommends authenticating PRACK like other SIP requests.
